info.title: Mind2Flow API
info.description:
Public REST API for building, managing and executing AI agents, multi-agent crews, devices, custom Python tools and scheduled tasks on the Mind2Flow platform.

Authenticate with a REST API key (created in the dashboard under Developers → API) sent as `x-api-key: rest_...` or `Authorization: Bearer rest_...`.

tags.name: Agents
tags.description: Create, manage and execute AI agents

tags.name: Tools
tags.description: Custom Python tools and sandbox execution

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Identity, profile (editable), account context, the account LLM keys, and Credits & History read-only: balance, payments, active plan, credit prices. Buying credits or a plan happens in the console.

tags.name: Magic
tags.description: TENANTS: Magic packages (agents, crews, custom tools of your organisation cloned into each signup), their signup links (each with its url) and redemptions. Scopes tenant:read / tenant:write. Credits per signup come from your balance and need confirm: true; so do deletes. Command Center items are console-only.

tags.name: Analysis
tags.description: Operational figures, conversation reading and search, LLM analysis and configuration diagnostics for your agents. Scope: agents:read. Organization-wide reads additionally require the TENANT or ADMIN role and are confined to your own customer.

tags.name: Artifacts
tags.description: Documents built from typed blocks — reports, test runs, prompt changes — whose figures are resolved from the database by the server, never typed by a model. Versioned; shareable by a public link that hides customer details by default. Scopes: agents:read / agents:write.

tags.name: Panels
tags.description: For external panels (a CRM, an inbox): subscribe to a WhatsApp device's traffic through a signed webhook and send through it. Available when panels are enabled on the server.

tags.name: Voice
tags.description: Phone calls with your agents (Twilio ConversationRelay, on your own Twilio account). Connect Twilio and pick a number once in the console (AI Agents → agent → Voice); then place calls, change the voice or greeting, pause the line and read calls here. Billed at 1 credit per 15 s of AI talk time (see /voice/pricing); Twilio bills minutes and numbers to your Twilio account. Scopes: agents:read / agents:write.

tags.name: Tenant
tags.description: White-label reselling: clients (accounts, subaccounts, users), credits and the signup form, pricing and the tenant Stripe, LLM keys lent to clients, per-account model defaults and log export, branding and custom domain. /tenant/admin/* is for platform administrators (role ADMIN). Scopes: tenant:read / tenant:write. Secrets come back masked; deletes, credit moves and admin actions need confirm: true.

tags.name: Dashboard
tags.description: The console Dashboard reporting: consumption, credits and costs, LLM token usage, per-subaccount metrics, organisation agents. Read-only, scope agents:read. A plain user sees its own account; a tenant its clients (accountId / subaccountId filters are checked).

tags.name: Apps
tags.description: External apps (Composio): find them, connect accounts (a sign-in link the account owner opens, or a key), and attach them to agents with PUT /agents/{agentId}/apps. Scopes: agents:read / agents:write.

tags.name: Knowledge
tags.description: GraphOS temporal knowledge graph: sources, ingestion, hybrid query and graph exploration. Scopes: knowledge:read / knowledge:write. Requires an OpenAI key on the account (BYOK) for ingestion and query. Agent graphs: add ?agentId=<one of your agents> to any of these routes to work in that agent's own graph instead of the shared one — create a source, upload files (recorded on the agent, which makes it read its own graph), sync, confirm columns, records, query, manual facts; deleting a source there removes it from the agent. GET /knowledge/graph/namespaces lists the agents that have one.

get.summary: Aggregated operational figures for an agent
get.description: Volume, distinct people, conversation depth, hour-of-day distribution (UTC), channels, response-time percentiles and errors, over a date range. Computed from the database, so these figures are exact. Read `notes` back to whoever sees the numbers: it reports when people could not be counted (activities recorded before sender tracking shipped carry no sender id), when messages came from the agent's own scheduled tasks, and when the range held more rows than were read.

get.summary: Find which conversations mention given terms
get.description: Per term: how many DISTINCT CONVERSATIONS and how many messages matched, plus the session ids. Per matching conversation: which terms hit, with snippets. Several terms in one call, because "how many people asked for each of these ten products" is one question. Matching is literal substring: case-insensitive but ACCENT-SENSITIVE, so "credito" does not match "crédito" — pass both spellings as separate terms. Per-term counts double-count a conversation that matched two terms; use `matches.length` for the de-duplicated number.

post.summary: Ask an arbitrary question of an agent's conversations
post.description:
You supply the question AND the fields you want back, so "which products did people ask for", "did this end in a sale" and "what went wrong" are all this one endpoint. Conversations are read in batches, so a month that would never fit in one context window is a handful of passes. Returns a value per conversation plus a frequency table per field.

COST: this is the only endpoint here that spends. It runs an LLM on YOUR account's own key (or the trial key while that is active) and answers 402 when the account has neither — it is never billed to anyone else. Keep `maxConversations` to what the question needs.

Values are extracted by a model reading text, so they can be wrong or missed. Hard figures belong to /summary, which is computed from the database.

parameters.description: Agent id, or "all" for every agent you own

question.description: What to determine about each conversation, in plain language.

fields.description: The values you want back per conversation, up to 8. Each becomes a column and a frequency table.

put.summary: Set the agent's apps and build what they need to run
put.description: toolkits replaces the agent's app list. selectedActions (omit to keep the current ones, max 128) and pinned [{toolkit, connectedAccountId}] (universal agents only; omit to keep) are optional. Builds the Composio servers the runtime needs — an agent with apps listed but not built loads none. Anything that could not be set up comes back in warnings; integrations is the live check (same as GET /agents/{agentId}/integrations). POST /agents and PATCH /agents/{agentId} do the same when toolsConfig.knowledgebase.composio.toolkits is sent, answering with apps and appsWarnings.

get.description: The Composio toolkits the agent is configured to use, the account pinned per app, how many actions are selected, the account's live connections, and `issues` — where configuration and reality disagree (pinned to an account that no longer exists, connected but not ACTIVE, apps with no actions selected). When Composio cannot be reached, `connections` is null and `notes` says the check did not run. That is not the same as "disconnected". `issues` holds real problems only.

get.summary: How the agent can be reached, and whether each way works
get.description:
Input and output channel, the API endpoint, the assigned WhatsApp device with its number and the date of the last inbound message, and the shared link with its active flag, expiry and request count. `issues` lists what is broken.

WhatsApp is probed LIVE: `whatsapp.liveState` is "open" when connected. When the probe cannot run, `liveCheck` is "failed" and `notes` says so; the stored `isConnectedFlag` can be stale, so weigh it against `lastInboundAt`.

put.summary: Subscribe a panel to a device
put.description: From now on every message the device receives or sends (agent replies included), every delivery status and every connection change is POSTed to `url`. Each delivery carries `X-M2F-Timestamp`, `X-M2F-Event`, `X-M2F-Delivery` (stable across retries — use it as an idempotency key) and `X-M2F-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with the returned secret>`. A device has one subscription; calling this again replaces the URL. A device that no agent answers is reserved for the panel (mode `inbox`): while subscribed it cannot be assigned to an agent, and unsubscribing frees it. A device an agent already answers stays with it (mode `agent`). Messages are delivered at least once — after a gap (a restart, or the first event of a device) the missed ones are recovered and sent with `replayed: true`, so deduplicate on `message.id`. Status and connection events are not recovered.

status.description: needs_mapping: a spreadsheet held until its column mapping is confirmed (PUT /knowledge/sources/{id}/schemas/{filename}).

record_count.description: Spreadsheets only: rows that reached the graph

webCall.description: Whether the page shows the call button

status.description: ACTIVE works; INITIATED = sign-in not completed

header.description: Column header as written in the file — send it back unchanged

field.description: Attribute name on the stored row

filled.description: Read-only: share of rows with a value (0–1)

invalid_count.description: Read-only: values that do not parse as the type

KnowledgeTabularSchema.description: How a spreadsheet is read. GraphOS proposes one on upload and holds the file until it is confirmed.

reason.description: Why it still needs confirmation; drift = the file's columns changed

duplicate_count.description: Rows sharing a name collapse into one entity

conflicting_count.description: Of those, rows whose values disagree

columns.description: Every column of the proposal, edited; field names of included columns must be unique

name_field.description: Must be the field of an included column

entity_type.description: What each row is: Product, Property, Service…

status.description: Set to inactive to pause the agent: it stops answering on its channels until set back to active.

CrewBlueprint.description: A crew in plain terms. Give either `steps` or `team` (a crew that is one orchestrator and its team). Agents are referenced by id and must be active.

inputDeviceId.description: WhatsApp input: the device the crew answers on

outputUrl.description: API output: where the answer is also POSTed

CrewBlueprintTeam.description: An orchestrator: the lead decides which members to ask (1–5, the lead not among them) and writes the answer.

lead.description: Agent id of the lead; it thinks with its agent's Thinking model

parallel.description: Ask independent questions at the same time (default true)

CrewBlueprintStep.description: Exactly one of: `agent`, `team`, `if`, `switch`, `apiSend`, `whatsappSend`. `apiSend`/`whatsappSend` come right after an agent step. A nested `if`/`switch` is the last step of its branch.

interactive.description: Ask the user until the step is done

interactionType.description: The builder Interaction Type (default user-approval when interactive); setting it makes the agent interactive

humanExpert.description: Phone of a human who answers (HITL)

doneKeywords.description: Comma-separated words that end an interactive step

body.description: JSON object or string; supports {{previous_output}} and other variables

responseMapping.description: Dot path of the response to pass on, e.g. result.id

CrewDelegation.description: One question an orchestrator asked a team member, and the answer

currentQuestion.description: A paused run: the question waiting for an answer

notified.description: A paused run: whether whoever must answer was told

inputData.description: The message, sender, channel and threadId of the run

outputData.description: finalOutput, replyTo and, for a paused run, waitingFor and question

stepResults.description: Per-step results, with an orchestrator's delegations

secret.description: Verifies X-M2F-Signature. Stable for the device.

mode.description: "inbox": people answer through the panel — the device had no agent and is now reserved for the panel. "agent": a Mind2Flow agent (or crew) answers; the panel follows the conversation and can write too.

agent.description: The agent that answers, in agent mode (null when a crew does). Pause or resume it with PATCH /agents/{agentId} { "status": "inactive" | "active" }.

message.description: Text, or the caption of a media message

PanelEvent.description: Body of a webhook delivery. Exactly one of message / status / connection is present, per `type`.

omitted.description: True when the file was too large to embed

url.description: Instead of base64, for a message that was sent by URL

error.description: On a failed message, the reason the gateway gave (Cloud API numbers)

replayed.description: True on a message recovered after a gap instead of seen live. It may repeat one already delivered: deduplicate on message.id.

raw.description: The gateway's original payload, without media bytes

enabled.description: false = paused: callers hear that the number is not available

voiceName.description: Catalog name, null for a voice outside the catalog

voiceGender.description: How `voice` sounds; used when voices take turns

alternateVoices.description: Voices that take turns with `voice`, one per call. Empty = `voice` answers every call

email.description: After each call: summary, the details the caller gave and the transcript, by email

voice.description: Catalog id (el-cristina), name (Cristina) or an ElevenLabs voice id

voiceGender.description: How `voice` sounds. With alternateVoices, the agent speaks of itself to match the voice on each call

alternateVoices.description: Replaces the list. [] = one voice. Each item: a voice as in `voice` (or { voice, gender?, greeting? })

greeting.description: Omit to use the line greeting

phoneNumber.description: E.164 number already in your Twilio account; creates the line if the agent has none

email.description: Email each call. `to` replaces the list (up to 10); enabling needs at least one address

outboundGreeting.description: What the agent says when the callee picks up an outbound call ("" = wait and introduce itself)

language.description: es-MX, en-US… or "multi" (automatic; needs ElevenLabs voices)

hints.description: Words the transcription should expect (names, products)

provider.description: "auto" (recommended for calls), "" (the agent's own) or a provider

whisper.description: The person hears who is calling and why before connecting

fallback.description: Nobody answered: back to the agent, or hang up

schedule.description: When the agent answers incoming calls (phone and PBX). Off = always. Outside it the call is refused before it is answered (no cost; the caller hears busy). Turning it off keeps the hours and closed days

answer.description: "outside" = only outside office hours and on closed days; "inside" = only during office hours

week.description: Office hours per weekday, Sunday first; [] = closed that day. Replaces the week

closedDays.description: Holidays, every year: "MM-DD" or a range "MM-DD/MM-DD". The office is closed all day. Replaces the list

webCall.description: Call button on the agent's shared link and embed (creates/removes pieces in your Twilio)

sip.description: Calls forwarded by the customer's PBX or phone provider over SIP; then GET …/sip-credentials

auth.description: "credentials" (default) = the provider signs its calls with the user and password; "ip" = calls are accepted from allowedIps only, for providers that send no user (Zadarma). The address does not change

VoiceLineConfig.description: Every setting of the line, as the console shows it. Secrets are reported as set, never returned.

schedule.description: enabled, answer, timezone, week, closedDays — as in VoiceLineUpdate

callStatus.description: Twilio final state: completed, no-answer, busy, failed, canceled

aiSeconds.description: Talk time with the AI (what is billed)

outcome.description: solicita-cita, informacion, recado, transferida, queja, sin-interes — or the Twilio state (no-answer, busy, failed) when the call never connected

data.description: What the caller said about themselves (name, email, what they want…), e.g. { "nombre": "Laura Gómez", "presupuesto": "900.000 €" }. null on calls made before this existed

message.description: Message sent to the agent on each run
